pairs.left: I. Provided the elastic limit is not exceeded, the extension is directly proportional to the force applied
II. A floating body displaces its own weight of fluid in which it floats
III. Any object partially or totally immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust which is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object

IV. When pressure is applied at any point on the surface of a fluid contained in a closed container, the pressure is transmitted undiminished to all parts of the fluid and to the walls of the container
V. Energy can neither be created nor destroyed but it can be transformed from one form to another

questions.content: A form one student uses a vernier caliper to measure the internal diameter of a 100ml measuring cylinder. What are the steps used by this student to get the readings?

media.alt: Unchanged original Physics question paper, page 6.
Unchanged original Physics question paper, page 7.

questions.marksProvenance: Moshi DC accompanying source marking guide, page(s) 3.
questions.markIncrementProvenance: Source explicit half-mark allocations where indicated; otherwise independently prepared self-assessment increments within the source maximum.
questions.answerKey: 1. Close the jaws to check zero and note any zero correction. 2. Insert the internal jaws inside the measuring cylinder. 3. Open them gently until they touch opposite inner walls across a diameter, without forcing them. 4. Keep the caliper aligned across the diameter and read the main scale just before the vernier zero. 5. Find the vernier division that coincides with a main-scale line. 6. Multiply that division by the least count. 7. Add the main-scale and vernier contributions and apply the zero correction, recording the internal diameter with its unit.
questions.markingGuide: Source allocation: 7 marks. Independently corrected internal-diameter rubric: 1 each for zero check/correction, use of internal jaws, gentle contact across opposite inner walls, aligned main-scale reading, coinciding vernier division, division×least count, and corrected total with unit. Accept equivalent valid measurement procedures. This replaces the defective external-jaw procedure in the source guide, not the question.
questions.solutionProvenance: SomaSmart independently prepared and checked internal-diameter procedure, correcting the external-jaw procedure in the source guide; source maximum retained.

questions.content: Errors usually arise due to several reasons. Briefly explain the three common errors caused by improper reading of an instrument

media.alt: Unchanged original Physics question paper, page 7.

questions.marksProvenance: Moshi DC accompanying source marking guide, page(s) 3.
questions.markIncrementProvenance: Source explicit half-mark allocations where indicated; otherwise independently prepared self-assessment increments within the source maximum.
questions.answerKey: 1. Parallax error: viewing a pointer or graduation from an oblique direction makes it appear aligned with the wrong mark; place the eye normal to the scale. 2. Scale-interval reading error: assuming each minor graduation has the wrong value produces an incorrect reading; determine the value of a division from labelled graduations before reading. 3. Unit or decimal-place reading error: reading a centimetre scale as millimetres or recording a misplaced decimal changes the reported measurement; use the printed scale unit and correct place value.
questions.markingGuide: Source maximum: 3 marks. Independent correction: award 1 mark for each distinct valid error caused by improper reading together with an explanation, up to 3. The model gives parallax, misinterpreted scale intervals, and wrong unit/place value. Accept equivalent valid reading errors. The source guide names zero and instrumental errors, which need not be caused by reading; its unqualified list is not used as the scoring key.
questions.solutionProvenance: SomaSmart independently prepared reading-error explanations matching the unchanged question, correcting the source guide’s causal mismatch; source maximum retained.
